_how: For every `#NNN` token `test_no_closed_issue_pointers.py`'s scanner found in this package, `gh issue view <n> --json number,state,title` was run BY HAND against this repository on that snapshot's own capture date, and the `state` field recorded verbatim; the snapshot is re-captured in place rather than rewritten, so the dates are PER RE-CAPTURE (each re-capture's date and the entries it added are recorded in `_why`; the additions of 269, 301 and 432 were captured 2026-09-22), and `_captured` above records the snapshot's initial capture date. A number that is not a real issue is recorded as `NOT_AN_ISSUE` and excluded from the CLOSED rule with its reason stated in the test.
_why: There is NO NETWORK in this suite: `just check-py` runs offline and a guard that phoned GitHub would be a guard that goes green whenever the network is down. So the states are COMMITTED and DATED instead. The date is the load-bearing half — this snapshot answers 'was the issue closed WHEN the reference was written', which is the question TEST-29 actually asks, and it is deliberately not self-updating: an issue that closes tomorrow does not retroactively make yesterday's citation a defect, and a citation added tomorrow against a stale snapshot is caught because the scanner requires every number it finds to be recorded here. Re-capture with the command in `_how` when a reference is added, and say in the commit why the new number's state is what it is.
